Why it is here: useful information for home safety

A smoke alarm going off in the basement isn’t all that useful if you can’t hear it when you’re sleeping upstairs. That’s one big reason why wireless interconnected smoke alarms are worth looking into. This becomes all the more important if you live in a larger or multi-story home.

If you’re looking to add an additional layer of security and some peace of mind to your home safety setup, this Black Friday deal on a six-pack of X-Sense SC07-W smoke and carbon monoxide alarms makes upgrading a lot easier on the wallet. Right now, the bundle is down from $270 to just $210 on Amazon, saving you $60 through Nov. 30.

The SC07-W does more than just detect smoke. This combination alarm system includes carbon monoxide monitoring, giving you protection against two types of household hazards in a single device. The biggest selling point here, however, is the ability to wirelessly connect up to 24 alarms.

If one alarm detects smoke or CO in—for example—the basement, every connected alarm sounds off together, making it much less likely for you to miss an alert. You also don’t need to mess around with additional wiring, making this an easy retrofit for an older home.

The product is designed for longevity and X-Sense has clearly paid a lot of attention to detail. Each alarm ships with a 10-year sealed battery, so you won’t have to keep track of battery replacements across multiple rooms. The built-in LCD displays carbon monoxide levels and alarm information, giving you all necessary information about what’s happening in your ambient environment instead of leaving you guessing.

Additionally, the alarm runs an automatic self-check every minute, which is a reassuring feature in a device as critical as this. Moreover, the X-Sense SC07-W is ETL certified and meets the latest US safety standards for smoke alarms.

If your current setup consists of standalone alarms scattered around your home, or no alarms at all, this Black Friday deal is a solid opportunity to cover multiple rooms and get interconnected protection at an affordable price.

item.title: PS5s Are in Short Supply for Black Friday, but You Can Still Buy One
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: informative on the PS5 availability

There may be a ton of Black Friday deals on electronics, toys, and gadgets out there, but don't get your hopes up if you're looking for a PlayStation 5. Not only are they not discounted, but the combination of international chip shortages, high demand caused by the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, and the general holiday shopping frenzy has also made it nearly impossible to purchase a new, unbundled PlayStation 5 at any price—nearly impossible, but not impossible.

Major retailers are fresh out of PlayStation 5 consoles

Whether you're looking for a PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, a PS5 with a disc drive, or the flagship PlayStation 5 Pro, you won't find them at major online retailers. PlayStation Direct lists all three consoles as "currently unavailable." Best Buy suggests making an account with them to "improve your odds" of getting one. I can't find a listing for a new PS5 on Amazon either.

You still have some options for obtaining a PS5, but none of them are great. Many refurbished PS5s are selling for well above the list price of a new unit. There are some bundled, special editions available, but you'll likely be paying a ton for those. If you're willing to get your hands dirty by dealing with the wild west of Facebook Marketplace, you might be able to track down a used PlayStation 5 at a reasonable price, but approach with extreme caution.

How to get the best price on a refurbished PlayStation 5

If you're looking for a refurbished PlayStation 5, the best way to avoid a headache is to focus on who did the refurbishing. Buying refurbished electronics directly from a manufacturer is generally safer than buying from a third party, and in this case, it's cheaper too. PlayStation Direct is offering a "Certified Refurbished PlayStation 5 Console" for the relatively reasonable price of $519, while a refurbished Slim sells for $499. But if you're in the market, I'd lock it in quick: PlayStation Direct is already out of refurbished PS5 Pros.

Amazon's Renewed program has some strict requirements for third parties to stay in the program, like keeping defect rates under 0.8%, but refurbished PlayStation 5s are going for a premium on Amazon at the moment. A quick look at the site reveals that the price of a refurbished PlayStation 5 is hovering near $900; a refurbished PS5 Slim will run you somewhere around $750, and the current average price of a refurbished PS5 Pro has ballooned to over $1,700. These are well above the retail prices of $649 for the standard version, $599 for the digital version, and $899 for the flagship Pro version of the PlayStation 5.

Buying a bundled PlayStation 5 console is costly as well

There are some bundled versions of the console listed for sale online too. If you buy one of these, you're getting a new console and some other piece of hardware or a game, but there's a ton of upcharge at the moment. They're generally more expensive than the original price and more expensive than refurbished units as well. Here are some examples:

- Best Buy lists this PS5 Pro with PlayStation Portal Remote for $2,134.99.

- GameStop lists a Ghost of Yotei Gold Limited Edition PS5 bundle for $769.99 ($731.49 for GameStop Pros).

- Best Buy lists a PS5 Slim with an external drive for $979.99.

Buying a PlayStation 5 on the used market

By far the largest used market for anything in the U.S. is Facebook Marketplace, including PlayStation 5s. I checked out my local Marketplace, and there are a lot of listings for the console within a 40-mile radius of Los Angeles. The average price of used PS5 consoles here is hovering between $300 and $500, which seems fairly reasonable. But with Facebook Marketplace, the number of potential red flags rises with the demand for the product.

I've bought and sold a fair number of things on Marketplace with no problems beyond the occasional flaky person, and I've written a list of hacks for the service, but I wasn't covering a "shortage buying" situation like this. Scams tend to rise with demand, so when I see a listing for a $150 PS5 console (that contains the text "$250 or best offer"), I'm suspicious. It could have been posted by someone who doesn't know what they have, but I wouldn't count on it. If you're buying a PS5 on Marketplace, check the model and generation details very carefully against the actual item. Make sure the seller is offering what you want and not a PlayStation 4 with PS5 games. Verify how it was stored and the condition it's in. But it ultimately can come down to vibes: Don't let your desire to score a PlayStation 5 get in the way of your gut check about the seller or situation.

Black Friday FAQs

Are Black Friday deals worth it?

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

How do I make the most of Black Friday?

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

item.title: These MAMMOTION Robotic Lawn Mowers Are up to $800 Off for Black Friday
item.description:

Why it is here: promotional content

Mowing the lawn is one of those homeowner chores that never gets less annoying—more so if you have a sizeable lawn. Keeping the grass in check can take up most of your weekend, but like a robot vacuum taking the brunt of your housework duties, a robotic lawn mower can do the yardwork for you.

Right now, MAMMOTION is offering substantial Black Friday savings on its LUBA lineup of lawn mowers, bringing the LUBA mini 2 AWD 1500H down to $1,599, from $1,999. Meanwhile, the more powerful LUBA 3 AWD 3000 is down to $1,999 from its usual $2,799. Both deals include a free mower wash stand, valued at $79. That’s up to $800 of combined savings, and the offers run through Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

If you’re picking between the two lawn mowers, your choice largely depends on the size of the area you’re mowing. The LUBA mini 2 AWD 1500H is designed for small and medium-sized yards, with a 360-degree LiDAR navigation system to map out your lawn and identify obstacles. The all-wheel-drive system can tackle slopes of up to 80%, and the side-mounted cutting disc helps it get closer to walls, fences, and flower beds.

For larger properties, the LUBA 3 AWD 3000 is a solid fit. This lawn mower includes the same 360-degree LiDAR navigation system, but pairs it with 4G-based Network RTK functionality and AI vision, so the mower stay on course without boundary wires or a separate antenna. It can also handle slopes as steep as 80%, and its 15.7-inch cutting width and two cutting discs can handle up to 5,400 square feet per hour. The AI vision system allows it to recognise and avoid 300 different types of obstacles, including toys and pets.

Both mowers are designed to remove much of the manual work associated with yard maintenance. Once configured, these mowers can manage multiple mowing zones, customize schedules, and varied cutting heights.

Priced at $1,599, the LUBA mini 2 is a fairly substantial investment, but the $400 Black Friday discount and free wash stand make it a bit easier to justify. Similarly, the LUBA 3 gets a more significant $800 savings, plus the wash stand. If you’ve been considering a robotic lawn mower to bring some automation to the outdoors, these Black Friday offers are worth a look.
